answer: Delayed-Audit Queue Positions. Each identity must harbor a queue slot that ages only while its owner performs verified work; new slots start empty. Matching or transacting requires a slot older than a threshold, so a fresh clone waits the full aging period before any utility. The attacker pays that waiting time per identity and cannot parallelize it across clones. A sable dashboard shows slot age publicly. Sybils also occupy scarce queue capacity, throttling the attacker's own throughput, while honest operators grow through a shared lagoon of audited history.
